title: 2010 HMMT February Combinatorics Problem 2
statement: How many positive integers less than or equal to 240 can be expressed as a sum of distinct factorials? Consider 0! and 1! to be distinct.

solutions.text: 39 Note that \(1=0!, 2=0!+1!, 3=0!+2\) !, and \(4=0!+1!+2\) !. These are the only numbers less than 6 that can be written as the sum of factorials. The only other factorials less than 240 are \(3!=6,4!=24\), and \(5!=120\). So a positive integer less than or equal to 240 can only contain 3 !, 4 !, 5 !, and/or one of \(1,2,3\), or 4 in its sum. If it contains any factorial larger than 5 !, it will be larger than 240 . So a sum less than or equal to 240 will will either include 3 ! or not ( 2 ways), 4 ! or not ( 2 ways), 5 ! or not ( 2 ways), and add an additional \(0,1,2,3\) or 4 ( 5 ways). This gives \(2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 5=40\) integers less than 240 . However, we want only positive integers, so we must not count 0 . So there are 39 such positive integers.
